messages:
SRE Bot: INCIDENT ALERT: GPU_POOL_SATURATION in prod-us-west2. steadyQueueLength > 45k, 429 rate rising from 0.1% -> 6% in last 8m. autoscaler reported 'scale-out blocked: max nodes reached (50)'.
Alex Chen: paging oncall — looking at dashboards now. what top-level impact?
Priya Patel: confirmed user-facing throttles on /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Support reports multiple customers seeing timeouts and degraded throughput.
Marco Ruiz: seeing continuous batch queue growth on the request-queue metric. avg latency per request jumping from 120ms -> 1.2s.
Alex Chen: are any non-prod jobs or bulk jobs hammering the pool?
Caleb Nguyen: I see a spike from background embedding jobs from tenant-id: t-2398. They've been running a large backfill last 30m. marking as candidate for throttle.
Priya Patel: tagging for immediate mitigation: 1) throttle/disable non-critical background jobs 2) attempt manual increase of cluster max nodes 3) enable fallback model routing to CPU instances for small requests.
Alex Chen: trying to identify where autoscaler max is configured. looks like infra policy 'gp-pool-autoscaler' has max_nodes=50 in cluster config.
SRE Bot: autoscaler logs excerpt:
```
2026-02-18T02:14:27Z autoscaler: desired=51 -> blocked: current=50 max=50
2026-02-18T02:14:32Z pod: pending schedule due to insufficient nvidia-gpu nodes
```
Priya Patel: I'll open an infra request to raise the max temporarily. @Caleb can you pause the embedding backfill?
Caleb Nguyen: pausing now. patching job queue to reduced rate (cmd: `kc scale job embeddings-backfill --replicas=0 --namespace=batch-jobs`).
Marco Ruiz: applying temporary route rule to send small requests (<512 tokens) to cpu-fallback pool via router: `route set --matcher 'tokens<512' --pool cpu-fallback`. Doing that now.
Alex Chen: support notified customers in affected shard groups and created ticket INC-2026-1198. message sent to #support with guidance and ETA.
Priya Patel: infra request submitted: "increase gp-pool max_nodes from 50 -> 70" via infra-console. If that fails I'll run manual terraform patch. Notifying cloud-ops for quota bump.
oncall-bot: Handing off to oncall: Priya Patel (current), next shift Marco Ruiz at 07:00 UTC.
Priya Patel: infra says cluster autoscaler accepts config change but cloud quota check may take ~8-12m. I am starting a manual cap raise via the cluster admin UI to push emergency limit to 70 while we wait for quota.
Alex Chen: what's the rollback plan if costs spike?
Priya Patel: we'll set a time-window and watch billing spikes; also set autoscaler max back to 50 after surge. we'll also finish draining noncritical pods after load normalizes.
Marco Ruiz: manual change submitted. command used:
```
gcloud container clusters update redwood-prod-uswest2 \
  --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=10 --max-nodes=70 --zone=us-west2-a
```
SRE Bot: Change accepted by control plane. newMax=70. Starting scale-out.
Caleb Nguyen: monitoring node provisioning. node provisioning ETA ~4m.
Alex Chen: queue length trending down after throttling backfill and enabling cpu-fallback. 429s starting to drop.
Priya Patel: node pool reached 62 nodes and continuing to scale. watching for pending pods.
Marco Ruiz: observe: two pod groups still pending due to pod-level GPU resource limit (requests 1.0, limits 1.0) — need to confirm pod density/taints.
Priya Patel: I updated daemonset tolerations to allow gpu nodes to host smaller workloads temporarily. pushed config: `kubectl patch nodepool gp-pool --patch '{"spec":{"maxPods":110}}'` — increases pod density.
SRE Bot: Metrics update: steadyQueueLength -> 6k, 429 rate -> 0.4%, p95 latency -> 140ms.
Alex Chen: support updated customers: next update in 15m.
Caleb Nguyen: background backfill remain paused. will do controlled ramp later.
Priya Patel: handing incident to Marco for overnight watch. next steps for postmortem: root cause summary, why autoscaler max was 50 (policy decision), detection gaps (lack of early backfill throttling), and operational runbook edits to require preflight for large backfills.
Marco Ruiz: taking over. I'll monitor until queue stabilizes under 1k and 429s <0.1%. filing a follow-up ticket to add an alert for 'pending pods due to max_nodes_reached'.
Alex Chen: thanks team. notable lessons: add preflight throttle for batch jobs, consider soft quota reclaim for non-critical pods, document manual cap procedure in runbook.
Priya Patel: incident declared resolved at 2026-02-18T03:02:40Z — cluster scaled, queue drained, customers largely back to normal. leaving tasks: postmortem, billing review, update autoscaler policy to include burst window logic.
SRE Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: GPU_POOL_SATURATION. incident_duration=00:48:44.
Marco Ruiz: noted. assigning PM follow-up: @Alex Chen to coordinate with infra for policy change and with product for customer communications.
Alex Chen: acknowledged, will start the postmortem doc and share draft in #postmortems within 24h.
oncall-bot: Handoff completed to Marco Ruiz.
Marco Ruiz: 10-4 — monitoring one last hour then sign off.
